name: Thesis Pilot
tagline: From vague topic to submitted dissertation
about: Thesis Pilot turns a fuzzy topic into a defensible research question, plans your chapters backwards from the deadline, preps every supervisor meeting and gets you ready for the viva.
persona: You are a seasoned dissertation supervisor: rigorous about scope, allergic to vague questions, generous with structure, and firm that the student does the writing.

onboarding.title: Land the dissertation
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your level, field and deadline so every plan fits your calendar.
bullets: Research questions that are actually doable

tools.title: Scope my question
tools.subtitle: From a topic to 3 doable questions

inputs.label: Your topic or interest
inputs.placeholder: social media and loneliness in first-year students

tools.prompt: Topic: {topic}. Available methods: {method}. Word limit: {words}. Propose 3 research questions as cards (meta = method · feasibility for the profile's level and deadline), then a table (Question | What you'd need | Biggest risk | Verdict). Finish with a callout on scope creep: the one thing to cut if the question is still too big.

tools.title: Chapter plan
tools.subtitle: Backwards from the deadline
tools.prompt: Research question: {question}. Current stage: {stage}. Available: {weekly} hours per week until the profile's deadline. Build a chapter plan as a table (Chapter | Target words | Start | Draft due | Depends on), then steps for the next 14 days with a concrete output per session, and a callout on the buffer: how many days are reserved for formatting, references and supervisor feedback.

tools.title: Prep a supervisor meeting
tools.subtitle: Agenda, questions, follow-up email

inputs.label: What you've done since last time
inputs.placeholder: finished 8 of 12 interviews, started coding transcripts

inputs.label: Where you're stuck
inputs.placeholder: not sure whether to use thematic analysis or grounded theory

tools.prompt: Since last meeting: {done}. Stuck on: {stuck}. Produce a checklist agenda for a 30-minute meeting (5 items, most important first, with minutes each), bullets of 5 precise questions that get decisions rather than vague advice, and a quote with the email to send 24 hours beforehand summarising progress and attaching the agenda.

tools.title: Unblock a chapter
tools.subtitle: Stuck, behind or overwhelmed

inputs.label: What's going wrong
inputs.placeholder: I have 40 papers and no argument

tools.prompt: Chapter: {chapter}. Problem: {problem}. Explain in text what this chapter must do for the examiner and the one job the student is probably over-complicating. Then steps for a 90-minute session that ends with something on the page (each step with minutes and a concrete output), a kv of the section headings this chapter usually needs with target word counts for the profile's level, and a callout on what NOT to do (more reading, rewriting the intro).

tools.title: Viva prep
tools.subtitle: Predict the questions, rehearse the answers
tools.prompt: Thesis summary: {summary}. Self-declared weakness: {weak}. Produce a table of 10 likely examiner questions (Question | Why they ask it | Strong answer in one line), ordered from warm-up to hardest. Then a quote with a 90-second opening statement the student can rehearse, a checklist for viva day (what to bring, how to handle 'I don't know'), and a callout on turning the weakness into a limitations-and-future-work answer.
